types.oie_definition: An organization that provides goods or services for profit.
types.embedding_query_text: Company: An organization that provides goods or services for profit. Also called Corporation, Business, Enterprise.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: Google is a well-known corporation, and the example for Corporation includes Google.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

types.oie_definition: A good or service offered by a company for use or consumption.
types.embedding_query_text: Product: A good or service offered by a company for use or consumption. Also called Application, Software, Service.

chosen_type.label: Product
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are specific products offered by companies, aligning with the Product definition.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

types.oie_definition: A formal document presenting findings or analysis on a specific topic.
types.embedding_query_text: Report: A formal document presenting findings or analysis on a specific topic. Also called Study, Publication, Research.

chosen_type.label: Report
chosen_type.justification: The mention 'BBC Verify report' fits the Report type as a formal document from an organization.

candidates.label: Report
candidates.comment: A Report is an Article generated by a governmental or non-governmental organization. Also called official report, document, publication. Examples: an annual financial report, a government research report, a UN policy report, a company's sustainability report.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: Thesis
candidates.comment: A scholarly document submitted by a candidate for an academic degree or professional qualification. Also called dissertation, academic paper, research thesis. Examples: a PhD dissertation, a master's thesis, an undergraduate honors thesis.

candidates.label: Article
candidates.comment: An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column. Examples: a newspaper article about local politics, a magazine feature on travel, a scientific journal article, a blog post. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.

types.oie_definition: A machine learning model designed to perform AI-related tasks.
types.embedding_query_text: AI Model: A machine learning model designed to perform AI-related tasks. Also called Algorithm, Neural Network, Model.

chosen_type.label: AIModel
chosen_type.definition: A machine learning model designed to perform AI-related tasks.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate captures AI models specifically; SoftwareApplication is the closest parent.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

candidates.label: 3DModel
candidates.comment: A 3DModel, as a MediaObject under CreativeWork, represents some kind of three-dimensional content, which may have various digital encodings. Also called 3D content, digital model, virtual model. Examples: A CAD file of an engine part, a character model for a video game, a geospatial terrain model, an architectural rendering.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: DefinedTerm
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.

types.oie_definition: A category of data or information used for analysis or representation.
types.embedding_query_text: Data Type: A category of data or information used for analysis or representation. Also called Data Format, Information Type, Data Source.

chosen_type.label: Dataset
chosen_type.justification: Satellite imagery is a structured collection of data, fitting the Dataset definition.

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

candidates.label: Text
candidates.comment: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Dataset
candidates.comment: A Dataset is a structured collection of information or data, typically organized for analysis or use. Also called data collection, data compilation, data repository. Examples: A spreadsheet of sales figures, a database of customer information, a collection of scientific measurements. Distinct from DataCatalog, which is a collection of multiple datasets.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

types.oie_definition: A specific functionality or component within a product.
types.embedding_query_text: Product Feature: A specific functionality or component within a product. Also called Tool, Function, Module.

chosen_type.label: ProductFeature
chosen_type.definition: A specific functionality or component within a product.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate matches 'Lens feature'; PropertyValue is the closest parent for features.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: ProductModel
candidates.comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: ProductCollection
candidates.comment: A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set. Examples: a collection of books by an author, a bundle of software products, a set of kitchen utensils, a curated selection of wines.

types.oie_definition: An individual human being with a name and identity.
types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being with a name and identity. Also called Individual, Individual Person, Named Individual.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The mentions are distinct individuals, aligning with the Person type examples.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

types.oie_definition: A sovereign state or nation within a continent.
types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign state or nation within a continent. Also called Nation, State, Geographic State.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: Iran is a sovereign state, matching the Country type definition.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

types.oie_definition: A structure where governmental functions are conducted.
types.embedding_query_text: Government Building: A structure where governmental functions are conducted. Also called Public Office, Administrative Building, Legislative Building.

chosen_type.label: LegislativeBuilding
chosen_type.justification: UK parliament is a legislative body's location, fitting LegislativeBuilding.

candidates.label: GovernmentBuilding
candidates.comment: A GovernmentBuilding is a civic structure that houses government operations or services. Also called public building, state edifice, official premises. Examples: city hall, parliament building, courthouse, post office. Distinct from GovernmentOffice, which is a specific type of organization within a government building.

candidates.label: LegislativeBuilding
candidates.comment: A LegislativeBuilding is a government building civic structure where legislative bodies meet and conduct their work. Also called capitol building, parliament house, assembly hall. Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Courthouse
candidates.comment: A Courthouse is a government building where legal cases are heard and judicial proceedings take place. Also called court building, hall of justice, judicial building. Examples: Supreme Court of the United States, Old Bailey, local county courthouse.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.oie_definition: A specific place or position in space.
types.embedding_query_text: Location: A specific place or position in space. Also called Site, Position, Place.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: White House lawn is a specific physical location, aligning with Place.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: VirtualLocation
candidates.comment: An online or non-physical location where events can be attended, such as a webinar or online meeting. Also called online venue, remote location, digital space. Examples: a Zoom meeting room, a webinar platform, a virtual conference hall.

types.oie_definition: A large and permanent human settlement, typically with defined administrative boundaries.
types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement, typically with defined administrative boundaries. Also called Metropolis, Urban Center, Municipality.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: Gaza is a city, and 'Ukraine's capital' refers to Kyiv, which is a city.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

types.oie_definition: A structured group of people working toward a common goal.
types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people working toward a common goal. Also called Institution, Group, Entity.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Common Space is a named organization, fitting the Organization type.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

types.oie_definition: A classification of data or content based on its nature or purpose.
types.embedding_query_text: Data Category: A classification of data or content based on its nature or purpose. Also called Content Type, Information Class, Data Classification.

chosen_type.label: Class
chosen_type.justification: AI content is a category of data, aligning with the Class definition.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: DataType
candidates.comment: DataType is a fundamental classification for the kind of values that can be stored or manipulated, such as numbers, text, or booleans. Also called primitive type, data format, value type. Examples: Integer, String, Boolean, Float, Date.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

types.oie_definition: A specific technical component or characteristic of a system or tool.
types.embedding_query_text: Technical Feature: A specific technical component or characteristic of a system or tool. Also called Functionality, Technical Mechanism, Feature.

chosen_type.label: TechnicalFeature
chosen_type.definition: A specific technical component or characteristic of a system or tool.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate matches 'Invisible watermarks'; PropertyValue is the closest parent.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

types.oie_definition: Weapons, vehicles, or gear used in military operations.
types.embedding_query_text: Military Equipment: Weapons, vehicles, or gear used in military operations. Also called Warfare Tool, Combat Gear, Armed Forces Equipment.

chosen_type.label: Vehicle
chosen_type.justification: Russian tanks are military vehicles, fitting the Vehicle type.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Car
candidates.comment: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Motorcycle
candidates.comment: A vehicle that is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle. Also called motorbike, two-wheeler, scooter. Examples: a Harley-Davidson, a Honda CBR, a Vespa scooter. Distinct from MotorizedBicycle, which is primarily a bicycle with an assisting motor.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

types.oie_definition: A notable or historically significant structure or site.
types.embedding_query_text: Landmark: A notable or historically significant structure or site. Also called Monument, Historic Site, Iconic Structure.

chosen_type.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
chosen_type.justification: Great Pyramid of Giza is a historical landmark, matching LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.definition: A day of the week (e.g., Monday, Tuesday).
chosen_type.justification: Thursday and Friday are days of the week, not specific dates, requiring a new type.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

types.oie_definition: A vocation or occupation requiring specialized knowledge or skills.
types.embedding_query_text: Profession: A vocation or occupation requiring specialized knowledge or skills. Also called Occupation, Career, Specialized Role.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: AI-detection researcher is a profession requiring specialized skills, fitting Occupation.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: Specialty
candidates.comment: Any branch of a field in which individuals develop specific expertise, typically through significant study and effort. Also called area of expertise, specialization, discipline, field. Examples: 'Cardiology' as a medical specialty, 'Corporate Law' as a legal specialty, 'Artificial Intelligence' as a computer science specialty.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.
